title: Evacuation Inform Index (EII)
summary: A composite index and interactive world map that scores 104 INFORM Severity crises on the risk of evacuating against the risk of staying, for comparing crises at a strategic level.

contribution.roleNote: Summer 2026 Ethical Tech CoLab cohort project; Yorke advised.

narrative.problem: Comparing crises means weighing the danger of staying against the risk of leaving, yet INFORM publishes no coordinates, and whether the roads out are usable, the most decisive input to evacuation feasibility, is reported by no open global feed for conflict zones.
narrative.decision: Places every crisis at a curated location, labelled as a sub-national area, a reception area or a population-weighted country point, instead of offset country centroids that put about three quarters of points somewhere the crisis is not.
narrative.tradeoff: 65 crises remain country-level stand-ins, and six are flagged low-confidence because a more precise point could not be assigned without inventing one; road reports are pinned at the crisis, never at the blockage.
narrative.limitation: Weights are preliminary, pending AHP expert surveys; only monthly fatalities enter the conflict score, road status is keyword-derived from headlines, and the ratio is least informative for the severity-5 crises.
narrative.caveat: Not for advising anyone whether to leave, operational go/no-go, route selection or justifying a restriction on movement. One score per crisis, mostly country-level; the hosted site shows a frozen data snapshot.
